survey: A leather Western saddle is draped over a horizontal wooden fence rail, with a vertical post at the right of the card. The rail runs straight left to right, seen almost front-on. The saddle's long axis lies along the rail, with the horn at the left and the cantle at the right. The seat's top surface and the horn cap are seen from somewhat above. The front skirt hangs as a flat vertical panel facing the viewer, in front of the rail. The back skirt shows behind the rail, shifted a little to the right, which fits the far side. The rail passes between the two skirts, so the saddle straddles it with the seat sitting at the rail's top. A central strap with a metal buckle hangs from the front skirt and holds the near stirrup, whose loop faces the viewer and whose tread shows its top. The far stirrup hangs behind it, slightly to the right, matching the back skirt's offset. Overall the view is close to one camera, slightly above and in front.

errors.where: Fence rail compared with the saddle seat and stirrup treads
errors.what: The seat top, horn cap and stirrup treads are all seen from clearly above. The square rail they rest on shows only its front face, with almost no top face, as if seen at eye level. The rail's camera height doesn't match the saddle's.

fix: Show the wooden fence rail from the same slightly-high camera as the saddle: a thin strip of the rail's top face visible along its whole length, matching how the saddle seat and stirrup treads are seen from above.
